Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve
$y=2x-{sin}^{2}⁡(x)+\frac{1}{2},$
the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi }{4}$, as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=2x-{sin}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{2},$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi }{4}$ is

$$
A={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}(2x-{sin}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-1)=-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}(2x-{sin}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}(2x+\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-1)+\frac{1}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}(2x+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\,|}_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =(\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{16}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{3\pi }{4}))-(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =(\frac{9{\pi }^{2}}{16}-\frac{1}{4})-(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{16}+\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{{\pi }^{2}-1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The area of the region bounded by the curve y=2x−sin2⁡x+12, the x-axis and the lines x=π4 and x=3π4 is A=∫π/43π/4(2x−sin2⁡x+12)dx.

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the sin2 term: cos⁡2x=1−2sin2⁡x

We can rearrange the above formula as 12(cos⁡2x−1)=−sin2⁡x.

Hence, the area of the region is A=∫π/43π/4(2x−sin2⁡x+12)dx=∫π/43π/4(2x+12(cos⁡2x−1)+12)dx=∫π/43π/4(2x+12cos⁡2x)dx=(x2+14sin⁡2x)|π/43π/4=(9π216+14sin⁡(2⋅3π4))−(π216+14sin⁡(2⋅π4))=(9π216−14)−(π216+14)=π2−12.
